name: FastAPI
summary: A Python ASGI web framework that turns typed path-operation signatures into request validation, dependency execution, response serialization, and OpenAPI descriptions.

features.name: Typed path-operation contract
features.description: FastAPI registers path operations from Python callables and annotations, retaining path, method, response model, status, tags, dependencies, and schema metadata in APIRoute objects.
benefits: One callable declaration supplies executable and descriptive API information
Route metadata can be grouped and inherited through APIRouter
costs: Runtime behavior depends on Python annotation and model semantics
A contract can become coupled to framework-specific parameter conventions

features.name: Recursive dependency graph
features.description: FastAPI analyzes endpoint signatures into Dependant nodes, recursively builds sub-dependencies, and solves them before invoking the endpoint, with caching, overrides, generator scopes, and sync-to-threadpool adaptation.
benefits: Cross-cutting resources and security checks are composable as callable dependencies
Dependency results can be reused within a request according to cache keys
costs: Graph construction, scope rules, and teardown ordering add lifecycle complexity
Dependency resolution can obscure the direct call path

features.name: Pydantic request/response boundary
features.description: Request parameters and bodies are parsed and validated against typed fields and models, while response models serialize and validate returned values according to the registered operation contract.
benefits: Rejects malformed input before endpoint business logic
Produces structured schemas and consistent response serialization
costs: Validation and serialization add runtime work and model constraints
Custom or direct Response returns can bypass parts of the declared conversion path

features.name: OpenAPI route projection
features.description: Registered routes, parameters, request bodies, responses, security metadata, and model schemas are projected into an OpenAPI document and interactive documentation endpoints.
benefits: Makes the API contract consumable by documentation and client-generation tools
Keeps operation metadata near executable route declarations
costs: The projection has to represent Python runtime behavior in OpenAPI's schema vocabulary
Undeclared or direct response behavior may not be captured automatically

mathematical_views.model: Typed partial function over request state
mathematical_views.question: How do a path-operation signature and request inputs determine validation, endpoint invocation, and response construction?
assumptions: A route is a partial function from an HTTP request state to a response
Annotations and FieldInfo define input and output predicates
The view abstracts Starlette transport and Pydantic's internal schema engine

mathematical_views.question: How are nested dependencies ordered, cached, overridden, executed, and cleaned up around an endpoint?
assumptions: Dependant nodes form a directed acyclic graph for supported dependency declarations
Edges point from a dependent callable to its prerequisites
Generator teardown is modeled as scoped transitions and not as arbitrary Python side effects

mathematical_views.model: Contract projection from executable graph to OpenAPI schema
mathematical_views.question: Which parts of the executable route/dependency model are represented in the generated OpenAPI document?
assumptions: Route metadata and Pydantic models are source objects, and OpenAPI is a projection
The projection is explanatory and does not prove runtime/documentation equivalence for custom code
Unmodeled direct responses and external side effects are outside the projection

benefits: Executable declarations and API metadata stay close
costs: Annotations become part of runtime framework behavior
Resolution and cleanup order require explicit lifecycle reasoning
Model conversion adds work and can constrain custom response paths
Generated schema cannot fully describe arbitrary runtime behavior
